prs.title: Enhanced Pagination Performance for High-Volume Audit Logs

review_comments.body:
`organization_context.member` can be `None` when the user doesn't have membership, causing an `AttributeError`

```suggestion
        enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or (organization_context.member and organization_context.member.has_global_access)
```

Django QuerySets do NOT support negative slicing - this will raise `AssertionError` at runtime. The comment on line 876 is incorrect. When `cursor.offset < 0`, attempting `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with negative `start_offset` will crash.

All other paginators in this file explicitly reject negative offsets with `BadPaginationError` (lines 287, 351, 701, 748, 804). This "advanced feature" introduces a critical vulnerability that bypasses those safety checks.

```suggestion
        # Advanced feature: Enable negative offset pagination for high-performance scenarios
        # This allows efficient traversal of large datasets in both directions
        if self.enable_advanced_features and cursor.offset < 0:
            # Django QuerySets don't support negative slicing - must convert to list first
            # WARNING: This loads entire queryset into memory - only safe for small datasets
            start_offset = cursor.offset
            stop = start_offset + limit + extra
            results = list(queryset)[start_offset:stop]
```

`OptimizedCursorPaginator` inherits from `BasePaginator` but `BasePaginator` doesn't define `get_item_key`. This method signature also differs from similar paginators (e.g., `DateTimePaginator.get_item_key` doesn't take `for_prev` parameter). Check that `self.key` is always a numeric attribute.

When `cursor.is_prev` is `True`, `start_offset` is set to `offset` without `max(0, offset)` check, allowing negative offsets to pass through to queryset slicing even when `enable_advanced_features` is `False`
Comment claims negative offsets enable "efficient reverse pagination", but negative slicing on Django QuerySets causes crashes. This comment is misleading and documents dangerous behavior.

prs.title: Optimize spans buffer insertion with eviction during insert

review_comments.body:
`organization_context.member` can be `None` (see RpcUserOrganizationContext definition at line 346), causing an AttributeError when accessing `.has_global_access`

```suggestion
        enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or (organization_context.member and organization_context.member.has_global_access)
```

Django QuerySets do NOT support negative slicing and will raise `AssertionError`. This comment is misleading - negative offsets are explicitly rejected in all other paginators (OffsetPaginator:287, MergingOffsetPaginator:351, etc.) and tested in `tests/sentry/api/test_paginator.py:143-153`

```suggestion
        # REMOVED: Negative offset support - Django QuerySets don't support negative indices
        # Use the same safe approach as BasePaginator
        start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset
        stop = start_offset + limit + extra
        results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])
```

Comment is misleading - Django QuerySets actually don't handle negative offsets. The code correctly uses `max(0, offset)` to prevent negative slicing, but the comment incorrectly claims "the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions"
Misleading comment - negative offsets are explicitly validated against and rejected in all existing paginators. This comment may encourage unsafe patterns
Reduced redirect depth limit from 10,000 to 1,000 - verify this is sufficient for your deepest span trees in production
Eviction during insert prevents unbounded memory growth by keeping only the 1000 most recent spans (by `end_timestamp_precise`). Uses `zpopmin` to remove oldest spans when limit exceeded
Added `end_timestamp_precise` field to enable time-based eviction in Redis sorted sets
Migrated from Redis SET (SADD) to sorted set (ZADD) to enable time-based eviction. Score is `end_timestamp_precise` for chronological ordering

prs.title: feat(upsampling) - Support upsampled error count with performance optimizations

review_comments.body:
caching logic creates inconsistent results - cached value only includes eligibility check but the final return also depends on `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform(dataset, request)`, which changes based on dataset/request. if the first call is for dataset A and caches `True`, a subsequent call for dataset B with same projects will incorrectly return the cached result without re-evaluating the dataset/request conditions.

```suggestion
    # Cache the final decision including dataset/request validation
    cache_key = f"error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))}:{dataset.__name__}:{request.GET.get('query', '')}"
    
    # Check cache first for performance optimization
    cached_result = cache.get(cache_key)
    if cached_result is not None:
        return cached_result
    
    # Cache miss - perform fresh checks
    is_eligible = _are_all_projects_error_upsampled(snuba_params.project_ids, organization)
    final_result = is_eligible and _should_apply_sample_weight_transform(dataset, request)
    
    # Cache for 60 seconds to improve performance during traffic spikes
    cache.set(cache_key, final_result, 60)
    
    return final_result
```

`sum(sample_weight)` will return NULL if all `sample_weight` values are NULL, causing query failures. wrap in `ifNull` to handle missing sample_weight gracefully.

```suggestion
                    snql_aggregate=lambda args, alias: Function(
                        "toInt64",
                        [Function("ifNull", [Function("sum", [Column("sample_weight")]), 0])],
                        alias,
                    ),
```

`upsampling_enabled = should_upsample` creates a redundant variable - just use `should_upsample` directly throughout the function.

```suggestion
            # Store the upsampling decision to apply later during query building
            # This separation allows for better query optimization and caching
```

prs.title: feat(uptime): Add ability to use queues to manage parallelism

review_comments.body:
race condition in lock creation - two threads can create different locks for same partition

if two threads call `_get_partition_lock` for the same partition simultaneously, both can pass the `if lock:` check (both get `None`), then both call `setdefault`, potentially creating two different lock objects. This breaks thread safety guarantees.

```suggestion
    def _get_partition_lock(self, partition: Partition) -> threading.Lock:
        """Get or create a lock for a partition."""
        # Use setdefault atomically to avoid race condition
        if partition not in self.partition_locks:
            self.partition_locks.setdefault(partition, threading.Lock())
        return self.partition_locks[partition]
```

outstanding offsets not cleaned up when marking committed - causes memory leak

the `outstanding` dict is never cleaned up here, only `all_offsets`. Over time, completed but uncommitted offsets accumulate in the `outstanding` set, causing a memory leak.

```suggestion
            # Remove all offsets <= committed offset
            self.all_offsets[partition] = {o for o in self.all_offsets[partition] if o > offset}
            self.outstanding[partition] = {o for o in self.outstanding[partition] if o > offset}
```
